title: e2e-latency-profiling-traces-2025-11-12
content:
Summary:
This note contains end-to-end latency traces collected during a production-like stress run focused on single-request generation latency (non-streaming full response) and per-stage breakdowns. Goal is to identify dominant contributors to p95/p99 tail latency and propose mitigations for the serving runtime (batching, routing, KV cache, model execution).

Test configuration (representative):
- Date range: 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-12 (sampling window)
- Model: open-weights 7B-class transformer (quantized int8 path in runtime)
- Hardware: Dedicated GPU pool (A100 equivalent), mixed instance sizes in pool
- Prompt/response shape: prompt ~128 tokens, expected response ~256 tokens (avg)
- Client pattern: bursty PLG traffic, median concurrency 60, peak concurrency 220
- Batching config: dynamic batching with max_batch_size=32, max_batch_latency_ms=25
- KV-cache: enabled for conversation reuse; observed hit-rate ~48% across traces
- Sample size: 18k completed requests (filtered out failures/timeouts)

Instrumentation & methodology:
- Traces include high-resolution spans for: ingress(http+auth), routing(policy+model-selection), batching(queue+wait), kv-cache(restore/attach), model-exec(kernel time), tokenization, serialization/egress.
- All spans recorded at service boundary by otel collector (server-side only).
- p50/p95/p99 computed from end-to-end request latency (client-received full response).
- Additional breakdowns computed by summing span durations per request and taking percentiles.

Overall E2E latency (full-response):
- p50: 1.20s
- p95: 2.90s
- p99: 5.60s
- Notes: distribution is heavy-tailed due to batching wait times under bursty arrivals and occasional kernel fallbacks on non-ideal instance assignments.

Per-stage p50/p95/p99 (median numbers across same sample):
- Ingress (HTTP + auth + parsing): p50=8ms, p95=12ms, p99=25ms
- Routing (policy lookup + model selection + hot-path checks): p50=3ms, p95=10ms, p99=30ms
- Batching (enqueue + wait for batch formation): p50=6ms, p95=220ms, p99=820ms
- KV-cache (restore + attach; hit path): p50=2ms, p95=6ms, p99=25ms
- Model execution (kernel time across all tokens; includes decode loop): p50=900ms, p95=2.3s, p99=4.0s
- Tokenization / detokenization: p50=5ms, p95=12ms, p99=30ms
- Serialization / egress (including final network send): p50=10ms, p95=20ms, p99=50ms

Per-stage contribution to p95 (rough percent of total p95 latency):
- Model execution: ~56% (1.62s of 2.9s)
- Batching wait: ~25% (0.72s of 2.9s)
- KV-cache & misc infra (ingress+routing+tokenize+egress): ~19% (0.55s)

Observations / root causes:
1) Batching tail is the single largest non-model source of p99 tail: when bursts push arrival variance up, many requests wait the full max_batch_latency_ms before being dispatched which inflates p95/p99. The batching wait distribution is bimodal.
2) Model-exec variance: p99 is disproportionately affected by a mixture of kernel selection fallbacks and low-SMT instances. On ~7% of requests we observe kernel fallback events that increase exec time by 1.3–2x. These correlate with instance heterogeneity and certain sequence length spikes.
3) KV-cache impact: cache hits reduce model-exec by ~30–40% (observed median exec time 900ms -> 620ms with hit). However, the global hit rate (~48%) means many requests still pay full model cost.
4) Small overheads (ingress, routing, tokenization) are stable and negligible for p50/p95 but add up across many calls.

Detailed trace patterns (examples):
- Typical fast path (p50): ingress 8ms + routing 3ms + batching 6ms + kv 2ms + model 900ms + other 15ms => ~934ms total (rounded 1.2s because distribution includes other variance).
- High-tail example (p99): ingress 20ms + routing 30ms + batching 820ms + kv miss 25ms + model fallback 4.0s + egress 50ms => ~4.95s (matches observed p99 bucket).

Impact of batching config experiments (A/B runs):
- Reduced max_batch_latency_ms from 25ms -> 10ms: p95 improved from 2.90s -> 2.1s, p99 improved from 5.6s -> 4.2s, but throughput dropped ~12% and CPU utilization increased on GPUs due to smaller average batch sizes.
- Increased max_batch_size from 32 -> 48 (same latency cap): slight p50 improvement (1.20s -> 1.05s) but p99 unchanged; increased variance in batching wait because larger batches take longer to fill.

KV-cache microbench:
- Cache hit path model-exec p95: 1.4s vs miss path model-exec p95: 2.3s.
- Actions: increase cache TTL for short conversations; opportunistic prefix caching for templates increased hit-rate by +7% in a small pilot.

Kernel fallback correlation:
- Kernel fallback events traced to two causes: (a) non-optimal quantization path selected for certain layer dims, (b) runtime kernel selector hitting an unsupported vector width on a small subset of GPU drivers.
- Fallbacks accounted for ~7% of requests but ~28% of model-exec p99 mass.

Recommendations (short-term / tactical):
- Set SLO-aware batching: implement adaptive max_batch_latency tuned by incoming qps to avoid long waits in burst windows. Owner: Jordan Patel.
- Enforce instance homogeneity for low-latency tier: route latency-SLO requests only to a homogeneous subset (identical kernel capabilities). Owner: Marcus Lee.
- Kernel selector hardening: add unit tests for layer dimension corner cases and add telemetry to flag fallback triggers early. Owner: Sofia Martinez (applied-ml + serving-runtime).
- KV-cache ops: increase TTL and enable prefix caching for templated prompts to boost hit rate. Owner: Product-hosted-api + eng-serving-runtime.
- Short-term deploy: lower max_batch_latency_ms to 10ms for the low-latency tier, with traffic-shift experiment and throughput monitoring. Owner: Release Eng.

Longer-term / strategic:
- Investigate model-sharded execution and early-exit heuristics to reduce model-exec tail for long outputs.
- Expand auto-scaling of dedicated low-latency pool to reduce queuing pressure under burst.
- Explore lighter-weight quantization kernels (int4) vs int8 tradeoffs to reduce kernel time while monitoring quality regressions.

Next steps & action items:
- (T+3 days) Run canary with SLO-aware batching on 10% of traffic; collect 72h traces and compare p95/p99. (Jordan)
- (T+7 days) Create an instance-homogeneity routing policy and pilot with a subset of customers suffering high tail. (Marcus)
- (T+14 days) Kernel-selector patch + additional telemetry rollout. (Sofia)
- (T+21 days) Re-run full profiling window and publish updated trace summary to Confluence with attached flamegraphs and span breakdowns. (Anita)

Appendix: raw numbers (selected quantiles)
- End-to-end: p50=1.20s, p75=1.65s, p90=2.30s, p95=2.90s, p99=5.60s
- Model-exec: p50=900ms, p75=1.2s, p90=1.8s, p95=2.3s, p99=4.0s
- Batching wait: p50=6ms, p75=18ms, p90=60ms, p95=220ms, p99=820ms

Notes / known limitations:
- Traces are server-side only; client-side network variance not captured (we used consistent internal test clients to reduce noise).
- Model used is representative but not identical to all production models; absolute numbers will vary by model size and quantization profile.
- Some telemetry misses exist for ~0.5% of traces due to transient exporter backpressure; those were excluded from percentiles.

If you want the flamegraphs and span-level raw JSON, see linked Confluence page (SERV-4321) or ask and I can attach the artifact to this doc.
